Eleanor Grace Whitfield was born on March 4, 1941, in Springfield, the second of four children of Walter and Ruth Hale. She grew up on the family farm at the edge of town, where she learned to bake bread, mend almost anything and find joy in the simplest things. She graduated from Springfield High School in 1959.
After earning her teaching degree, Eleanor spent thirty-four years teaching second grade at Lincoln Elementary School. Generations of students remember her patience, her gentle humor and the way she made every child feel seen. In 1963 she married her sweetheart, Robert Whitfield, and together they built a home filled with music, laughter and the smell of something good in the oven.
Eleanor loved her garden, her church choir and long Sunday drives through the countryside. She volunteered at the public library for many years and never missed a grandchild’s recital or ball game. She was happiest with a cup of tea, a good book and her family close by, and her kitchen table always had room for one more.
She was preceded in death by her beloved husband, Robert, and her brother, Thomas. She is survived by her children, Susan Ellis (Mark) and James Whitfield (Laura); five grandchildren; two great-grandchildren; her sisters, Margaret and Anne; and many nieces, nephews and dear friends. Her kindness, her faith and her laughter will live on in all who knew and loved her.
The family thanks you for joining us today.

Robert James Carter was born on June 12, 1948, in Riverside, the eldest of three sons of Harold and Mary Carter. He grew up fishing the river with his father and fixing anything with an engine, and he graduated from Riverside High School in 1966.
Robert served four years in the United States Navy before starting a thirty-eight-year career with the county water department, where he was known for his steady hands and his terrible jokes. In 1971 he married the love of his life, Linda Reyes, and together they raised three children in the house on Oak Avenue.
He coached Little League for twenty summers, sang bass in the church choir and never met a stranger. He was happiest in his workshop, on the lake at sunrise or at the head of a crowded Sunday table, telling the same stories everyone loved to hear again.
He was preceded in death by his parents and his brother, Edward. He is survived by his wife of fifty-five years, Linda; his children, Thomas Carter (Anna), Karen Wallace (Mike) and William Carter; seven grandchildren; his brother, George; and many friends. His faith, his humor and his generous heart will be missed by all who knew him.
The family thanks you for joining us today.
